Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment focuses on the generation of spliced and non-spliced peptides by proteasomes to identify HLA-A*02:01 restricted epitopes. While 'targeted MS' is mentioned via the use of an inclusion list, the acquisition mode is explicitly stated as DDA (Top 20). The assay is fundamentally immunopeptidomics as it targets the HLA-I immunopeptidome.

noncellular_sources: 20S proteasome was purified from peripheral blood
scope: 20S proteasome was purified from peripheral blood as follows: (i) 10 ml peripheral blood was homogenized, lysed and centrifuged; (ii) the supernatant was fractionated by ammonium sulfate precipitation (35% and then 75%); (iii) the latter pellet was fractionated by chromatography on DEAE-Sephacel; (iv) the selected fractions were separated by 10–40% sucrose gradient and followed by (v) anion exchange chromatography on Mono Q in an Akta-FPLC system; (vi) the selected fractions (2–4 mL) were further purified by DEAE-Affi-gel-blue chromatography.
Synthetic polypeptides (40 μM) were digested by 3 μg 20S proteasomes in 100 μl TEAD buffer

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The proteomics experiment analyzed the products of in vitro digestions of synthetic polypeptides using purified 20S proteasomes. The proteasomes were isolated from human peripheral blood via a multi-step purification process including chromatography and sucrose gradients. While the text mentions cell lines (GR-LCL, HCC1143, HCT116, SW480) and human PBMCs, these were either used for in silico model development, TAP assays, or are mentioned as previous/external data (PXD000394), not as the material analyzed in the primary MS experiment (PXD015580).
